subject: Verdant AI — geographic processing, subprocessors, and cross-border transfer details
messages:
From: Maya Rodriguez <maya@verdant-ai.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Quick Q: where will Verdant data be processed / cross-border

Hi Rachel,

We’re evaluating Redwood for an inference endpoint that will process EU customer prompts and a subset of uploaded documents (some contain PII). Before we get too far I have a few quick questions from legal/security: 

- Which regions do you actually process request payloads in (not just control plane)?
- Which subprocessors will see payloads (cloud providers, logging, monitoring, analytics)?
- Do requests ever transit the US or other territories even if processed in EU?
- What are default retention windows for prompt/response logs and how can we request deletion/certification?

We’re a small pilot so a concise answer / any diagrams would be perfect. If it helps, I can loop in our security lead.

Thanks,

Maya Rodriguez
Sr. Privacy Counsel, Verdant AI
maya@verdant-ai.com


From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rodriguez <maya@verdant-ai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 13:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where will Verdant data be processed / cross-border

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. High level answers first, then specifics and attachments. I’ve attached our current processing map and the subprocessor inventory for your review.

Summary (short):
- Regions: Hosted Redwood routes inference jobs to the region you select in the API/console. For EU customers we can pin requests to EU compute regions (EU-WEST / West-Europe). Hosted customers default to region-based routing, but some auxiliary services (control plane, monitoring indexers) may run in the US; see detail below.
- Subprocessors: Primary compute is on major cloud providers (AWS eu-west-1, GCP europe-west1, Azure westeurope) depending on capacity and instance types. Logging/analytics/usage telemetry is handled by our EU-only stack when customer pins EU residency; backups and cross-region replication are opt-in. Third-party monitoring (Datadog) and observability traces are restricted to EU endpoints for EU residency customers.
- Transit: We endeavor to avoid transiting the US for EU-pinned workloads. However, ephemeral routing (DNS, load-balancing) can cause packets to touch intermediate networks. We treat transit differently than processing: processing occurs on EU compute nodes when EU residency is requested, and we do not persist payloads in US systems for EU-residency customers.
- Retention & deletion: Default retention for Hosted (non-dedicated) telemetry/requests is 30 days token-level logs and 90 days for aggregated usage metrics. We offer shorter retention windows and deletion-on-demand via our Data Deletion API for customers on paid tiers. For Dedicated/Private deployments you can set retention to match your policy and we will support certified deletion requests (we provide deletion receipts).

Details / evidence: see attached redwood_processing_map_202705.pdf and redwood_subprocessors_202705.csv — those list the current cloud regions and active subprocessors. A couple of implementation notes:

- Residency modes: Hosted (default) / Dedicated (reserved capacity) / Private (VPC / air-gapped on-prem). For EU data residency choose either Dedicated reserved pool in eu-west or our Private deployment inside your VPC.
- KMS & key ownership: For Hosted EU-pinned customers we run with customer-managed keys where required (BYOK on Dedicated/Private). Keys are region-scoped and HSM-backed for enterprise customers.
- KV/prefix caching: We never persist raw user prompts beyond the configured retention window. KV caches are in-memory on the serving node; they are evicted on instance termination and not written to long-term storage.
- Subprocessor list: includes cloud compute (AWS/GCP/Azure), monitoring (Datadog EU endpoints), S3-equivalent backup (object storage in EU if residency requested), and a SaaS telemetry ingestion partner (only for aggregated metrics). The CSV includes addresses and contract dates.

Next steps: If you want a short tech call we can walk through the processing map with our security engineer (Monica) and Marcus from our sales team to discuss tradeoffs and a proposed DPA amendment for EU residency.

Best,

Rachel Kim

From: Maya Rodriguez <maya@verdant-ai.com>

Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where will Verdant data be processed / cross-border

Rachel — thank you, that is helpful. A couple of clarifying points from our security lead: 

1) For the Hosted EU-pinned case: can you confirm that backups/replication are not copied to US object storage by default? The CSV suggests some cross-region replication is possible.
2) For deletion certification: what is the SLA for issuing a deletion certificate and what format does it take? We need something that our auditors will accept (time-stamped, scope of deletion).
3) If we decide to pilot on Hosted EU-pinned but later move to Dedicated, will you be able to migrate history and provide a migration plan (we’d likely want to delete history in Hosted after cutover).

Also — can Marcus propose 30/60/90 day retention buckets we can choose between?

Regards,

Maya

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rodriguez <maya@verdant-ai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 16:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where will Verdant data be processed / cross-border

Maya — answers inline and next steps below.

1) Backups/replication: By default we do not replicate EU-pinned customer object backups to the US. Cross-region replication is opt-in and controlled by the residency setting and backup policy. The subprocessor CSV has a "replication_allowed" column — for EU-pinned accounts that column is set to "no" for US regions. If you see entries suggesting replication, that is for multi-region redundancy customers who explicitly opt in.

2) Deletion certification SLA and format: Enterprise customers receive a deletion certificate within 72 hours of a certified deletion request. The certificate is a PDF that includes: timestamp(s), scope (objects/rows/logs deleted), account/deal id, and the operator’s audit id. For Dedicated/Private we can deliver a signed deletion manifest per cluster and coordinate on-chain certification where customers require cryptographic attestations.

3) Migration from Hosted -> Dedicated: Yes — we provide a migration playbook. Typical pattern: export and transfer via secure S3 transfer into your Dedicated pool, run a validation job, and then issue a hosted deletion certificate. We provide a dry-run and optional escrow window. We’ll include the migration steps in the DPA addendum.

Retention buckets (proposed by Marcus):
- 30 days (default): minimal logs and request payload retention; good for short pilots.
- 90 days: balanced — default aggregated metrics retained longer.
- 365 days: for customers who need longer telemetry for analytics; available on Dedicated with cost adjustment.

Marcus can follow up with pricing delta for each bucket and any impact on SLA. Monica and I can run a short security call (20–30 minutes) this week if you’d like. Are you available Thursday 12:00–12:30pm PT or Friday 9:00–9:30am PT?

Regards,
